subject: PO formatting, invoice cadence & net terms for Brightline onboarding
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@brightline.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: 2026-08-30T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: PO format + net terms for Redwood subscription

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — excited to get Redwood live for our NLP pipeline. Our procurement team has a few mandatory requirements before we can process a vendor:

- All invoices must reference a Purchase Order number in the invoice header and include the Brightline Entity ID and Project Code (we'll attach our PO template).
- Standard payment terms are Net90 for SaaS vendors; our default is Net90 unless credit/finance approves otherwise.
- We require monthly invoices aligned to our month-end close (we close on the 5th of each month) — invoices should be split between two cost centers and delivered as two separate invoice documents.
- We do not have EDI setup for new vendors; we prefer PDF invoices uploaded to our vendor portal.

Can you confirm Redwood's ability to: accept our PO template (attached), produce split monthly invoices, and discuss net terms? If Net90 is not feasible, what alternatives do you offer and any discounts or prepayment options to bridge the gap?

Attaching our PO template: Brightline_PO_Template.xlsx

Thanks,
Sara Kim
Procurement Manager | Brightline Systems
Sara.Kim@brightline.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@brightline.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO format + net terms for Redwood subscription

Sara — really appreciate the clear list. We can work with most of this but need to align on a couple of items. Quick answers up front:

- PO fields: we can include PO number, Entity ID and Project Code in the invoice header. Could you confirm exact field names as they appear in your ERP (so our AR mapping matches)?
- Split invoices: we can issue two separate PDF invoices per month to match cost centers, though our billing engine will still track the subscription as a single contract for SLA/discount purposes.
- Net terms: our standard for self-serve + enterprise is Net45. Net90 is outside our default credit box but possible with finance approval and a commercial adjustment. I’ve looped in Vivek (Finance) to propose options.

I attached a short PO spec that maps Brightline fields to our invoice headers: Redwood_PO_Spec_v2.xlsx — can you validate?

Proposed next steps:
1) Vivek to outline approval path for Net90 vs midpoint options (Net60 + discount, or Net90 with holdback/fee).
2) You confirm exact ERP field names and monthly cutoff (you noted 5th — good to confirm timezone and whether that’s business-day adjusted).
3) We draft a one-page amendment to the MSA capturing invoice cadence and PO mapping.

Thanks — I can jump on a 20-min call if it helps move faster.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: PO format + net terms for Redwood subscription

On Fri, Aug 30, 2026 at 12:20 PM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed next steps:
> 1) Vivek to outline approval path for Net90 vs midpoint options (Net60 + discount, or Net90 with holdback/fee).

Vanessa / Marissa — quick finance perspective for the thread so we can give Brightline concrete options:

- PO formatting: we will require the PO number present on the first page of the invoice PDF and in the filename to support automated ingestion. The fields we need (exact mapping) are: PO Number, Entity ID, Project Code. The attached vendor onboarding checklist outlines our preferred file name pattern.
- Split invoices: technically supported. We will generate two distinct PDF invoices monthly and map amounts to the specified cost centers. Note: split invoices will be treated as separate documents but are reconciled under a single invoice run for revenue recognition.
- Terms options:
   * Standard: Net45 (no commercial adjustment).
   * Compromise: Net60 with 1.0% prompt-payment discount for annual commitment >= 12 months.
   * Net90: requires a credit review and triggers either (a) a 0.75% financing fee applied to the invoice, or (b) a 2% holdback withheld and released after final reconciliation for the period. Net90 approvals typically take 7–10 business days.

If Brightline wants Net90 with no financing fee, we would need a purchase order with a credit guarantee or a purchase card pre-authorization (rare). Otherwise the Net60 + 1% discount is the smoothest path from an ops/collection standpoint.

I’ve attached our vendor_onboarding_checklist.pdf that lists the fields and sample filename convention.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@brightline.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com, finance+vendor@brightline.com
Date: 2026-09-01T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO format + net terms for Redwood subscription

Vanessa / Vivek,

Thanks — I reviewed the options with our FP&A and we have the following constraints from a policy perspective:
- Net90 is the baseline for all new SaaS vendors unless an exception is granted by treasury. We don’t have budget authority for prepayment.
- We cannot accept any financing fee applied to invoices (that will block approval).
- A small discount against list is possible but we need alignment from procurement and sourcing. Our request: Net90 + 1.5% discount for the first 12 months (we can re-evaluate thereafter).

Operational asks:
- Invoice cadence: monthly split invoices delivered by the 5th business day after month-end (we close on the 5th).
- File naming: include PO number, Entity ID and Project Code in filename. I attached our filled PO template for your reference.

Attached: Brightline_PO_Template_filled.xlsx

If Net90 absolutely requires a holdback/fee, can Redwood structure the contract so the fee is captured as a short-term holdback that is released after 60 days? That would be more acceptable to treasury than an open financing line.

Thanks,
Sara

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@brightline.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO format + net terms for Redwood subscription

Sara — appreciate the clarity and the filled template. We want Brightline as a customer and can be flexible if we find a commercial compromise. Here’s a proposal that balances Redwood’s cash/credit exposure and Brightline’s procurement policy: 

Option A (preferred for Brightline ops): Net60 + 1.0% discount for a 12-month committed term. We will support split monthly invoices delivered by your 5th business day and ensure filename/field mapping matches the PO template. No holdback/fee.

Option B (if Brightline must use Net90): Net90 with a 2% holdback retained by Redwood and released 60 days after invoice date upon reconciliation; in exchange Redwood will give 1.5% discount for the first 12 months (to match your ask). Alternatively, we can do Net90 with a 0.75% financing fee (but I understand you cannot accept a fee on the invoice).

Operational items we need to finalize to lock this down:
- Confirm which option (A or B) procurement will accept.
- Confirm sample PO field names exactly as they appear in your ERP (we need to map to: "PO Number", "Entity ID", "Project Code").
- Sign a one-page amendment to the MSA that specifies invoice cadence, split-invoice handling, filename convention and the chosen terms. I’ve attached a draft amendment and the MSA redline: Redwood_MSA_amendment_draft.pdf.

If you’re okay with Option A (Net60 + 1.0% for 12 months), we’ll issue paperwork for signature today and kick off onboarding.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@brightline.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com, finance+vendor@brightline.com
Date: 2026-09-02T15:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO format + net terms for Redwood subscription

Vanessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. Procurement and treasury discussed and we are willing to accept Option A: Net60 + 1.0% discount for a 12-month committed term. That keeps our internal payment runway and is workable for treasury.

We confirm: monthly split invoices by the 5th business day after month-end, filename to include PO Number / Entity ID / Project Code, no financing fee. We will route an initial PO (using our filled template) through your vendor portal by EOD Monday and expect the signed amendment back from Redwood so our legal team can attach it to the PO.

Next actions for Redwood:
- Finalize the one-page amendment and send for signature (DocuSign link preferred).
- Confirm the invoice filename convention and provide a sample invoice after first billing run so we can validate ingestion.

I'll follow up with the PO submission. Looking forward to onboarding.

Best,
Sara Kim
Procurement Manager | Brightline Systems
